title: People and process: the controls that are held by humans

atom_notes.A14: most successful intrusion starts with a person, not a parser
atom_notes.A02: the trust boundary between an employee and a customer is the one nobody draws

required_cells.why: you cannot review a process you have not inventoried
attribution is the property that makes every other control auditable

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Offboarding access review
entries.role: What survives a departure. Accounts, tokens, device trust, shared passwords and local files each have their own lifecycle, and most reviews check only the directory account.
preconditions: a person has left or changed role in the last quarter
an inventory of systems exists or can be built
oracle: a credential or session still working after the last day, evidenced by a login record
every system on the inventory answered for, positive or negative
a shared credential rotated, because revoking one account does not revoke a shared secret

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Shared account and attribution audit
entries.role: Whether an action can be attributed to a person. A shared login makes the audit trail a guess, which is both a control failure and an incident response problem.
preconditions: the organisation has accounts used by more than one person
oracle: an action in the log that cannot be attributed to one human
one credential used from several distinct clients in a window
an access review that lists a person against an account they do not uniquely hold

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Credential storage outside a manager
entries.role: Where secrets actually live. Notes, chat, spreadsheets and screenshots are the real inventory, and a manager's adoption says nothing about what is outside it.
preconditions: the organisation has a password manager or policy
oracle: a working credential found outside the manager, with its location
the manager's coverage reported as a fraction of the credential inventory, not a yes

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Device trust enrollment path
entries.role: Whether a device can be enrolled outside the managed process, and what organisational data reaches a personal device that cannot be removed.
preconditions: access depends on device posture or enrollment
oracle: an unmanaged device treated as trusted, with the enrollment record or its absence
work data present on a device outside management, demonstrated on a real device

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Privileged access approval trail
entries.role: Whether elevated access is requested, approved and recorded per session. Standing privilege with no trail is indistinguishable from a compromised account until someone looks.
preconditions: the organisation has administrative access to production or data
oracle: an elevated session with no approval record
the approval record missing a second party, where dual control is claimed
duration of the elevation longer than the task required

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Disclosure programme scope and safe harbour
entries.role: The relationship with people who find things. Scope must be precise enough to test the real system, and good faith testing must be protected in writing.
oracle: a report marked out of scope for a real issue, which is a scope defect
the safe harbour statement read for what it actually protects
acknowledgement measured against the stated window on a real report

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Review depth on security relevant changes
entries.role: Whether authentication, payment and crypto changes get a different review than a typo fix, and whether a named owner exists for each sensitive path.
preconditions: the project has a review process and code ownership
oracle: a sensitive change merged with one approval and no security review
a sensitive file with no named owner
the repeat rate of the same class of mistake, which is the only honest measure of whether review teaches

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Credential lifecycle: reset authority, handover, support view
entries.role: Who can reset what, how a new starter receives their first credential, and what a support agent can see beyond the ticket. Each is a place where process replaces cryptography.
preconditions: the organisation has a support desk and onboarding
oracle: a reset completed by a single actor without a second approval, from the audit record
an initial password visible to a third party in transit
a support view exposing fields unrelated to the request

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Developer feedback loop and escalation reach
entries.role: Whether a developer learns that their change introduced a weakness, and whether a report reaches someone who can act out of hours. Both are process properties with measurable latencies.
preconditions: the organisation runs a review process and receives reports
oracle: the same class of mistake recurring, measured per team across engagements
time from report to a human acknowledgement, including out of hours
a finding that reached nobody who could act on it

tree.q: Is the question about who someone is, what they hold, or whether a process happened?
tree.why: Identity questions are answerable by probing. Process questions usually require being inside, which changes what is available.

branches.action: review the directory against the leaver list and look for shared credentials
branches.oracle: a login after the last day, or one credential from several clients

next.q: Is it a credential, a device, or an elevated session?

branches.action: search the places people actually keep them
branches.oracle: a live secret outside the manager, with its location

branches.action: compare the endpoint inventory against enrollment records
branches.oracle: a device without an enrollment record holding data

branches.action: read the approval trail for a real session
branches.oracle: an elevated session with no approval record

branches.action: read the review and disclosure records
branches.oracle: a step with no record, or a report that reached nobody

mirror.rule: one credential used from several distinct clients

mirror.attack: a credential found outside the manager
mirror.detect: secret scanning of chat and shared drives
mirror.rule: a live secret in a non manager store

mirror.attack: an unmanaged device treated as trusted
